page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-48 is an x86_64 server instance within the network-optimized family. Configured with 48 dedicated virtual CPUs and 180 GB of system memory, the instance delivers an allocation of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The configuration contains zero GPUs and provides no bundled local disk storage, necessitating the use of network-attached storage options for all persistent file systems.

From an architectural and resource perspective, the instance provides dedicated vCPU execution without thread contention from shared hosts. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators streamlines costs for deployments focused primarily on computational tasks and network throughput. However, workloads requiring heavy disk I/O must account for network storage latency, as all disk operations rely on attached block volumes.

Given its high core count and balanced memory allocation, Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-48 is well suited for network-intensive application servers, container orchestration nodes, backend API layers, distributed batch processing, and continuous integration workflows.
